title: That's Not Nice (1)
subtitle: Idioms for lies, tricks, and false promises.

idioms.mean: tell someone something untrue to trick them
idioms.ex: He said his phone was dead, but I think he was just **feeding me a line**.

idioms.mean: keep someone waiting with false promises
idioms.ex: She keeps saying "maybe next week". I think she's **stringing you along**.

idioms.mean: sweet talk or big lies used to fool someone
idioms.id: rayuan gombal / omong besar untuk menipu
idioms.ex: The salesman's speech about the "magic" phone was a total **snow job**.

tip: **feed someone a line** dan **string someone along** sering dipakai dalam bentuk continuous: *He's feeding you a line*, *She's stringing him along*. **Snow job** adalah kata benda: *That was a snow job*.

options: tell someone a lie to trick them
keep someone waiting with false promises
a job in a cold country
sweet talk used to fool someone
meaning.why: Rayuan atau omong besar untuk menipu.

dialogue.q: A: He told me he can't come because his grandma is sick… again. B: That's the fifth time! He's ___.
dialogue.why: Alasan palsu → feeding you a line.

dialogue.q: A: My boss keeps promising me a raise "next month". B: It's been a year. He's ___.
dialogue.why: Janji palsu terus-menerus → stringing you along.

dialogue.q: A: The seller said this cream makes you look 20 years younger in one day! B: Come on, that's a ___.
dialogue.why: Omong besar untuk menipu → snow job.

correct.q: "I believed his story, but later I found out he was feeding me a line."
"My mum fed me a line of rice for lunch."
correct.why: Salah: feed someone a line = membohongi, bukan memberi makan.

correct.q: "She always keeps her promises, so she's stringing us along."
correct.why: Salah: kalau janjinya ditepati, itu bukan string someone along.

correct.q: "Don't believe his snow job about making millions in a week."

speak.q: Has anyone ever fed you a line? What happened?
speak.model: Yes. A friend borrowed my motorbike and said he would return it in an hour. He came back at night and said the traffic was terrible, but I knew he was <mark>feeding me a line</mark>.
speak.label: feed someone a line

speak.q: Why is it unkind to string someone along?
speak.model: Because the other person keeps hoping. If you <mark>string someone along</mark>, they waste their time waiting for something that will never happen. It's better to be honest.
speak.label: string someone along

speak.q: Have you ever seen an advertisement that was a snow job?
speak.model: Yes, I saw an online ad for a drink that promised I'd lose ten kilos in a week. It was a complete <mark>snow job</mark>, so I didn't buy it.
speak.label: snow job

roleplay.situation: Temanmu sudah tiga kali membatalkan janji nongkrong dengan alasan yang aneh-aneh.
steps: **Student A:** ceritakan alasan anehmu ("my cat ate my phone charger…").
**Student B:** bilang kamu rasa temanmu bohong (*You're feeding me a line*).
**Student B:** jawab bahwa dia terus memberi harapan palsu (*Stop stringing me along*) dan janjinya itu *a snow job*, lalu tentukan hari yang pasti.
roleplay.target: Target: percakapan 1–2 menit, semua 3 idiom terpakai.
